transcript.reasoning:
Now correlate. OTDR A from site A: distance_km 29.691 reflective loss 3.64 dB, reflectance -29.2 dB. From site B: distance 0.006 km reflective loss 3.65 dB reflectance -29.6 dB. That corresponds to the same physical point near B-ODF. The route map: B-ODF at route_km 29.07. Distance from A to B-ODF is about 29.07 km + launch/receive cords? OTDR note: distances are fibre distances from ODF at shooting site. Launch and receive cords of 1.000 km used; receive cord ends in open connector. So the fibre distance measured is including the 1 km launch cord? Actually launch cord is 1 km at start? Let's interpret: Distances are fibre distances from ODF at shooting site. Launch and receive cords of 1.000 km were used; receive cord ends in open connector. That means the measurement includes the launch cord? Hmm typical OTDR measurement from ODF includes launch cord. They say launch and receive cords of 1.000 km were used; receive cord ends in open connector. So the distance to B-ODF from A should be about route 29.07 km plus maybe launch cord? Wait distance measured from ODF at A, so fibre path: launch cord 1 km? Or launch cord is used to separate connector? Let's think: The event at 29.691 km from A is close to 29.07 km route + 0.621 km excess? Could be launch cord offset. OTDR B shows event at 0.006 km from B ODF. That is essentially at the B ODF connector. The large reflective loss 3.65 dB is characteristic of a dirty or damaged connector causing reflection and insertion loss. Reflectance -29.6 dB is not very reflective? Typical good connector reflectance ~ -50 dB. -29 dB is higher reflection, indicating a problem.

The PM shows Rx power drop about 3.3 dB (from -11.1 avg to -14.35 avg). Tx stable. So link loss increased about 3.3 dB. OTDR shows 3.64 dB loss at B-ODF. That matches.

Also note patching work at site B ODF on 2026-10-21 02:31 UTC, just before alarm at 03:00. That points to connector at B-ODF (maybe B-ODF connector or patch panel). The link record has elements: B-ODF is connector (ODF/patch panel) at route_km 29.07. There is also B-ATT fixed in-line attenuator at site B between ODF and receiver, design value 5 dB. The OTDR event from B shows loss 3.65 dB at 0.006 km. That is very close to B ODF. Could be the connector at B-ODF or the attenuator? Attenuator is typically non-reflective. The OTDR shows reflective event. So connector.

Now need to decide fault type: dirty_connector vs damaged_connector. Connector end faces cannot be inspected remotely. For a connector fault submit dirty_connector with clean_connector unless evidence shows it is damaged: crew inspects, cleans, and replaces if damaged. Evidence: reflective loss 3.64 dB, high reflectance -29 dB, patching work recent, loss increase ~3.3 dB, matches. No evidence of damage like break. So we should submit dirty_connector with action clean_connector. Element id: B-ODF? Or maybe B-ATT? Let's examine OTDR A event 6 at 29.691 km reflective loss 3.64 dB reflectance -29.2 dB. OTDR B event 1 at 0.006 km reflective loss 3.65 dB reflectance -29.6 dB. That is the same connector. The route element at 29.07 is B-ODF. Element id is B-ODF.

Alternatively could be the connector at site B ODF between the patch panel and attenuator? The link record says B-ATT is fixed in-line attenuator at site B between ODF and receiver. So the fibre path from B-ODF to B-ATT to receiver. OTDR from B sees first event at 0.006 km, that could be the connector at the B-ODF panel. Might be B-ODF.

The fault type allowed: dirty_connector, damaged_connector, macrobend, bad_splice, fibre_break, wrong_attenuator, tx_degradation.

Dirty connector seems most plausible.
